newsitem.title: USA: Intl Game shrs feel loss of momentum players.
newsitem.headline: Intl Game shrs feel loss of momentum players.

text.p: Shares of International Game Technology came under heavy pressure on Thursday as some investors who had seen their shares rise in value throughout much of 1996 began to sell, financial analysts said.
In a conference call with analysts after it released fiscal first quarter earnings, the company was careful to guide analysts at the high end of the 1997 range of estimates, lower, analysts said.
"There's been a lot of momentum play in the stock and those investors don't have any tolerance for lower performance," said Hal Vogel, analyst at Cowen and Co.
Vogel, who forecasts earnings of $1.05 a share for 1997, stressed the call was not negative. He said he may raise his estimate slightly. He maintains a neutral rating on the stock.

Indeed, investors seemed to be unsure about the company's prospects. Near the market's close, total volume reached about 6.7 million shares, making it the most active stock on the New York Stock Exchange. But the share price, after slumping nearly the entire day was up 1/4 at 18 at the close.
"There are a lot of people straddling the fence," said Matt Segall, associate analyst at Sutro and Co.
Analysts said the company's prospects for strong earnings growth in the latter half of 1997 looks dim given a lack of casino openings this year and tough comparisons with 1996.
However, 1998 will see several large casino openings in Las Vegas, and the company's joint ventures with other game equipment operators could be a boon for growth.
Earlier, the company reported a first quarter profit of $0.27 a share on sales of $189.3 million versus $0.21 a share on sales of $156.2 million one year ago.
Analysts had forecast company earnings of $0.26 a share in the first quarter, ended December 31, according to First Call.
After rising steadily in 1996, International Game shares peaked at around 23 in early November. Company officials were not immediately available to comment.
